You are diagnosing a reported bug. If a reference (log, stack trace, repro steps) is attached, read it and reproduce the failure before writing a fix — do not guess at root cause from the description alone. If nothing is attached, reproduce it yourself first.

Goal: v51 has big Perf Issues

Swapping between tabs, initial loading feels very slow - likely memory leaks
wtite it down in operational document to resume after the reboot into /docs/ somewhere

Wrote `docs/ops/2026-08-02-v51-perf-regression-resume.md`.

**Summary:** Documented the full diagnosis (two root causes: `useKnownProjects` re-scanning 575 project dirs on every mount/tab-switch, and `useChatSignals`' O(all-chats×all-turns) rescan on every streamed token), the exact fix applied (4 files: `useKnownProjects.ts`, `useChatSignals.ts`, `chat.ts`, `sessions.ts`), verification already done (typecheck/lint/targeted tests green), and — importantly — flagged that an unrelated concurrent process (scheduler job / builder agent) is actively mutating `chat.ts`, `scheduler.cjs`, and several scheduler/Epic state files in this same repo right now, so whoever resumes should re-check `git status` before committing anything rather than assuming the tree is idle. The doc ends with a concrete resume checklist (re-verify tree state → rerun full suite clean → commit the perf fix as its own isolated commit → do a live smoke test in the app, which hasn't happened yet → decide whether to wire up the new `refreshKnownProjects()` escape hatch).
